DDInter1963.mechanism: When used concomitantly with copper-chelating agents for the treatment of Wilson's disease, zinc salts can compete with copper for chelation and renal excretion. The clinical significance is unknown, although reduced efficacy of one or both agents may theoretically occur. Zinc alone can reduce copper levels by blocking its absorption in the intestine and promoting fecal copper excretion.
